rationale: Act on the child question @q_phantom_claim_vote_decision by building its discriminator: a five-voter cluster in which the deposed leader and one follower keep an uncommitted suffix while the other three commit a newer term and publish a snapshot below that suffix, so both minority members become phantom holders; the same RequestVote (the stale follower's real log claim, with the leadership-transfer flag so the known-leader rejection cannot mask the log test) is then delivered to the phantom holder and to a majority voter whose cached state matches its snapshot. Local construction runs deliver both requests on the first attempt and show the predicted contrast (phantom grants, consistent voter rejects, candidate's last log term below the phantom's snapshot term), but those are construction feedback; the receipt is requested here. A new source range is declared for the requestVote declaration so the requirement can carry a verified anchor for the vote premise.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: the phantom log claim produced by the InstallSnapshot path changes how a server decides votes, because requestVote evaluates log completeness with getLastEntry, which prefers the cached claim over the installed snapshot. Source basis: getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry, state.go 160-174); requestVote's completeness test rejects only when the voter's last term is greater than the candidate's, or equal with a greater index (src_vote_log_check, raft.go 1725-1748 inside requestVote at 1626-1758); installSnapshot never resets that cached entry (src_install_snapshot_tail, raft.go 1837-1977). Consequence: a voter whose snapshot already contains committed entries in a newer term will still grant a vote to a candidate whose last log entry carries an older term, whenever the cached claim wins the comparison - exactly the case a voter comparing against its snapshot would reject. The scope is bounded rather than established as a safety break: the phantom suffix was never committed (a quorum storing it would have committed it), so its holders were a minority of the configuration that created it, and a leader's snapshot index cannot fall below committed history; a quorum of phantom voters therefore needs a configuration change that turns that minority into a majority of a new configuration. The affected direction is also milder than the phrasing 'stale rejection' suggests: the claim can both reject candidates whose last term equals the claimed term with a lower index and grant candidates whose last term is below the snapshot's term. Limits: this account is source-derived plus local construction feedback (the five-voter probe behaved as predicted: phantom granted, consistent voter rejected, candidate term below the phantom's snapshot term); it has no retained receipt yet, the vote effect is unmeasured in 3-voter configurations, and the configuration-change path that could turn phantom holders into a quorum is not measured at all.
counterevidence: The same root cause in the progress direction was measured to be bounded: starvation ends once a snapshot above the cached claim is published (parent question receipt), so the phantom claim is a transient state within a term, not a permanent log corruption.

A phantom suffix lies beyond the commit index of the term that created it, so its holders are a minority of that configuration; the parent account already argues that a quorum of phantoms then needs a configuration change, which no measurement here supports.
limitations: No retained receipt for the vote decision yet; the comparison set is requested with this update.

The probe delivers the request through another node's transport and uses the leadership-transfer flag, which is the path that removes the known-leader rejection; a plain campaign is rejected for the leader reason before the log test and would not discriminate.
Configuration changes, larger clusters and repeated phantom generations are unmeasured.

scope.description: One five-voter history in one process: forty entries are committed on all five voters, the current leader and one follower are partitioned together and the leader appends a further forty entries that reach only that follower, so the pair holds an uncommitted suffix while the other three voters elect a new leader, commit twenty entries and publish a snapshot at an index below the suffix end. After healing, both minority members install that snapshot and become phantom holders. The same RequestVote, built from the stale follower's real cached claim and carrying the leadership-transfer flag, is then delivered to the phantom holder and to a majority voter whose cached state matches its snapshot.
assumptions: Fault model: no message loss inside the injected transport; the induced events are one partition of two voters from three, one clean retention of the minority suffix, and one explicit snapshot on the majority leader.

The stale candidate's claim is real (the follower really stores and caches the suffix it received from the deposed leader); the single supplied element is that its RequestVote carries the leadership-transfer flag, which is how a transferred-to or stale-transfer target campaigns and is what removes the known-leader rejection so the log test is reached.

Requests are delivered through another node's in-process transport with bounded retries, because a node's own transport has no peer entry for itself; retries only repeat the same single request payload.
Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport and MockFSM.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds test code.
Automatic snapshotting is disabled so the published snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

experiment.prefix: The harness elects a leader in a five-voter cluster, commits forty entries, partitions the leader with one follower, drives forty further applies on the deposed leader so the pair shares an uncommitted suffix, waits for the pair to stop leading, waits for one of the remaining three to be the only stable leader, commits twenty entries there and forces Snapshot(), then heals the partition and waits until both minority members have installed the snapshot (their last snapshot index becomes non-zero). It records the phantom claim, snapshot and applied indexes on the phantom holder and on the second minority member, the consistent voter's claim/snapshot/applied, the leader's snapshot, and the candidate's real claim, then builds one RequestVote with term = the consistent voter's current term + 1, last log index/term from the stale follower's cached claim and the transfer flag, and delivers it to the phantom holder and to the consistent voter, recording the responses and the derived booleans.
experiment.requirement: A voter's own log-completeness judgment for vote granting must not treat log entries the installed snapshot superseded as current, otherwise it can grant authority based on history it no longer holds.

comparisons.description: The phantom holder granted the vote request although its own installed snapshot already carries a newer term.
The voter whose cached state matches its snapshot rejected the same request, so the difference is the phantom claim rather than the request.
One identical request, two voters, different decisions in the same history.
The granted candidate's last log term is below the phantom holder's snapshot term, so the granted authority rests on entries the voter's snapshot superseded.
